title: POC sync: quality & rollback simulation with Orchid AI
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on recent quality regressions in the pilot, confirmation of rollback playbook, clarification on private VPC data retention, and agreement on bench test to measure latency/cost tradeoffs. Redwood to run rollback simulation and share results; Orchid to provide 500 edge prompts and a golden set for scoring.
action_items: Samir Patel: run rollback simulation on dedicated variant and capture perf traces (due 2026-08-24)
Lena Ortiz: share 500 representative prompts + golden answers spreadsheet (due 2026-08-21)
Maya Chen: send security RSA and SOC2 one-pager + private deployment notes (due 2026-08-20)
Iris Gomez: schedule a 60m deep-dive with infra team to review KMS/KV cache behavior (due 2026-08-26)
next_steps: Redwood to execute rollback drill on staging dedicated pool and send log bundle
Customer to provide labeled golden set and priority failure scenarios
Schedule follow-up demo with infra deep-dive next Wednesday
Agree on 2-week pilot extension if rollback metrics meet SLOs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-19 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Iris Gomez (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Tom Reeves, Nadia Park, Evan (Orchid AI)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda — quality regression update, rollback drill, security Qs, and next steps.
[00:23] Lena: yep, thanks Maya. quick note — we saw a bump in hallucination rate on monday for our support routing prompts, about a 6% increase in false positives.
[00:38] Tom: and it was during higher load, which is why we suspected batching or kv cache interactions, uh which might be doing something weird.
[00:52] Samir: ok, thanks. we dug into traces — saw an uptick in token truncation for longer context, and a mismatch when prefix caching combined with quantized variants, so the output distribution shifted. there may be a kernel fallback path that changed behavior.
[01:12] Nadia: can i ask, was this on hosted or dedicated? data residency question.
[01:18] Maya: that happened on hosted staging, not on your dedicated pool; but we did run a few dev experiments swapping in the q4-8 quantized build which could change generation slightly.
[01:30] Lena: so the concern is production parity — we don't want the hosted experiment to differ from what we see on dedicated when we scale.
[01:39] Samir: agreed. that's why the rollback simulation is important — we can force a variant switch and run the golden prompt set to measure differences.
[01:49] Evan: quick question about the golden set — we'll share 500 prompts, is that enough? we also want edge cases.
[01:56] Maya: 500 is a good start, if you add the top 20 failure patterns that's ideal. please include expected label/answer.
[02:06] Lena: okay, i'll collate and drop in the shared sheet (link: https://docs.redwood/example/golden-prompts). apologies the link is a placeholder but we'll post the real one.
[02:17] Samir: walk-through of the rollback playbook: 1) detect regression via scorecard threshold, 2) open canary to dedicated variant with pinned kernel, 3) run back-compat tests, 4) if pass then rollout, else full rollback. during the drill we'll capture token-level diffs and KV cache hit rates.
[02:36] Tom: is there an automated fallback if we hit capacity limits mid-rollback? like route to a cheaper model?
[02:43] Samir: yes we support policy routing — you can route by latency or cost and have an automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant, but for this simulation we'll keep routing simple.
[02:53] Nadia: security — when you capture traces for us, will those include PII? we need to ensure logs are redacted or stored in our VPC.
[03:01] Iris: good point. logs for the drill will be redacted and we can push them directly into your S3 under your VPC/priv infra using our private deployment connector. keys stay in your KMS/HSM.
[03:14] Nadia: okay that helps. also SOC2 evidence and audit logs?
[03:18] Maya: i'll send the SOC2 summary and the audit log retention options after the call.
[03:24] [03:24] Evan: slight aside — are there known regressions with certain quantization levels? we tried q4_0 and saw differences.
[03:33] Samir: briefly, q4_0 and q4_8 can shift token probabilities slightly — it's model plus kernel dependent. we keep per-model quant profiles in the catalog. for production we recommend validating on your golden set and we can provide recommended quant profiles.
[03:49] Lena: can we run a test of the production-ish dedicated pool? we want perf parity and check latency at 99p.
[03:57] Samir: yes, we'll run a dedicated benchmark — capture p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1K tokens. that'll be part of the rollback drill bundle.
[04:06] Tom: timeline?
[04:08] Maya: we'll start the rollback simulation Thursday (2026-08-20) morning PST, with results by Monday EOD. does that work?
[04:16] Lena: yes.
[04:17] Maya: okay next, quick demo of a single failure case Samir pulled up.
[04:22] [04:22] Samir: "here's prompt A, orig answer vs current. note the hallucinated entity — the model inserted 'Riverton' instead of 'Riveton' which triggers the routing misclassification".
[04:35] Lena: yep that's one of the bug classes. sometimes it's phonetic errors like 'K V cache' being read out — the transcript generator even messed it up.
[04:44] Samir: ha, yes our transcripts can say 'K V cash' — we saw that.
[04:48] Evan: what's the remediation? prompt engineering or guardrail?
[04:51] Samir: usually a mix — short term we add a post-filter and stronger named-entity guardrail; medium term we tune the quant/profile or pin to a kernel that maintains distribution.
[05:02] Lena: i want to see how false positive rate changes if we switch to a pinned kernel vs apply a post-filter. can you show a side-by-side?
[05:09] Samir: yes — the drill will include a side-by-side diff table and confusion matrix.
[05:15] Tom: any cost impact for pinned kernel?
[05:18] Samir: small uptick — pinned kernel might be 5-12% more expensive per token in our measurements but reduces variance and improves stability. we'll quantify it.
[05:28] [05:28] Iris: operational note — if we do a private deployment (VPC), we can reduce egress and compliance concerns; however, on-prem adds hardware ops overhead.
[05:38] Nadia: would we still get the same rollout tooling if we self-host?
[05:41] Iris: yes, our private control plane supports rollouts and can integrate with your KMS; some runbook steps change for on-prem but the dev experience is similar.
[05:50] Lena: regarding metrics — can we surface token-level hallucination markers to our dashboard?
[05:55] Samir: yes, we'll add a tag on the traces and expose an event stream to your observability stack — we can push to DataDog or your internal Kafka.
[06:05] Evan: competitors question — we evaluated VertexAI but found less explicit rollback tooling and harder kernel control.
[06:13] Maya: noted.
[06:15] [06:15] Samir: technical detail — during rollback simulation we'll capture: model variant id, kernel id, quant profile, KV cache hit ratio, avg prefix length, batch size distribution, and per-request token diffs. we'll attach a CSV and a replay script.
[06:32] Tom: will the replay include exact rng seeds to reproduce?
[06:36] Samir: we can capture seeds where possible, but deterministic reproduction across quant levels is tricky; we'll include best-effort replay and raw request/response payloads.
[06:46] [06:46] Lena: ok good. next — acceptance criteria for the drill? we propose: no more than 1% increase in false positives for the golden set at p95, latency p99 under 800ms, and rollback procedure completes within 10 minutes for canary.
[07:06] Maya: reasonable. we can instrument and report against those.
[07:11] [07:11] Nadia: legal side — we'll likely ask for an addendum about audit access and logs retention for the pilot.
[07:18] Maya: understood, i'll loop legal and send a template.
[07:22] Evan: quick operational ask — can you surface a heatmap of prompts by failure class? that'll help prioritize fixes.
[07:29] Samir: yes, we'll add a heatmap to the results bundle.
[07:34] [07:34] Maya: recap: Redwood runs rollback simulation, shares log bundle and metrics, Orchid provides golden set, Redwood sends SOC2 and audit docs, schedule infra deep-dive.
[07:45] Lena: agreed. thanks everyone.
[07:48] Maya: i'll send meeting notes and action items, and i'll set the follow up for next Wednesday 60m.
[07:55] Tom: thanks.
[07:57] [End of recording]
